## Pricing & Reviews
Rated 3.9 from 109 reviews.
Top review: I bought this for a house guest in a wheelchair (double amputee) to make our bathroom somewhat ADA compliant for her. She said it was perfect. At the lowest seat setting, it was parallel with the edge of my tub so she could slide right across. She loved having the back for stability since she has no feet to plant on the bathtub (she removed her prosthetic legs once situated in the tub before turning on the shower).The chair dried quickly. Suction cups works well and no slipping. VERY easy to assemble, no tools required. It held a 150 lbs person easily, I sat on it too and I'm 195 and it was very stable. I even wiggled around trying to make it slip or work the screws loose. We also measured the heck out of the bathtub (front, back and middle) before ordering to make 100% sure it would fit at the base since we didn't know if she preferred the chair in the back, front or middle of the tub in relation to the showerhead.The screws (more like wingnuts) are plastic (to avoid rust?) so I would recommend tightening them from time to time. I can see how hand-tightened screws that have no washers, lock nuts, screwlock or pins might come a little loose after repeated use."Screws fall out all the time, the world is an imperfect place."Please NOTE: This is a bench depth (front to back) and not a "chair" though I know it looks chair-ish. In a normal chair you can sit down and sit back and your knees bend at the front edge of the seat, your feet are flat on the ground, and the chair support your butt as well as under the thighs. Officially at 11.5" in depth, I'd guess this item is about half the depth (front to back) of a normal "chair" so your butt is supported (seated) but you kind of need good feet / legs to hold you in place or you would tip forward off the bench (or have to lean back all the time). It is a good width from left to right at 19.5" for a relatively "normal" sized person, but if you were much wider, it may be an issue. But I can't see how a "wider" seat could even fit in the bathtub with a shower curtain since this chair left no room on either side once in the tub.We were concerned after reading many reviews which is why we tested the EFF out of it, wanted to make sure it wouldn't collapse with our houseguest on it. Read some reviews where people said it collapsed. I truly can't see how that's possible the assembly was incorrect, the legs were not adjusted to the same height, OR it was defective or damaged (the tubing or the legs) in some way, thus compromising the structural integrity of the legs. Imagine trying to crush an empty can with downward pressure. If there are no dents in the side of the can, then it's difficult. If you dent the side of the can, then it collapses more easily at that point. Also, I can see it becoming weaker if one tried to spread the legs at the bend (to get a wider base?) thus weakening the integrity at the joint.I cannot speak to the issue of "rust" that happens according to some reviews since we didn't keep it after two weeks of daily use. I was concerned though so I did check the seat every day to ensure it was draining all the water. And finally, we made sure the rubber suction cup ends (feet?) were "flat" on the floor. They are angled somewhat so it mattered which legs go in the front/back and sides to ensure the feet are even to the floor.

The Drive Medical Shower Chair with Back is designed to bring stability, comfort, and safety to daily bathing routines for individuals who need extra support due to age, injury, surgery, or limited mobility. Drainage holes built directly into the seat help prevent water from pooling beneath the user, creating a cleaner and more stable seating area. These thoughtful features make the chair an excellent choice for homes seeking practical safety upgrades or for individuals returning from surgery and working to regain their independence.
